medications.purpose: Treat essential hypertension; first‑line per NICE NG136 for metabolic syndrome
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends an ACE‑I as first‑line antihypertensive in metabolic syndrome

medications.purpose: Reduce LDL‑C/non‑HDL‑C and lower cardiovascular risk in metabolic syndrome
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 advises statin therapy for QRISK ≥10% or metabolic syndrome components

medications.purpose: Add‑on to achieve BP target <140/90 mmHg per NICE NG136
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I + CCB combination when BP remains above target

medications.dose: 0.25 mg weekly, titrate to 1 mg weekly over 4 weeks
medications.purpose: Weight management in obesity (BMI ≥30) with cardiometabolic risk
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 lists GLP‑1 RA (semaglutide) as pharmacological option for BMI ≥30 with comorbidities

medications.dose: 500 mg once daily with evening meal, increase by 500 mg weekly to max 2000 mg/day as tolerated
medications.purpose: Treat pre‑diabetes / high risk of progression to type 2 diabetes
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 recommends metformin for pre‑diabetes with high cardiovascular risk when eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m²

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive antihypertensive effect may cause symptomatic hypotension, especially after initiation.
interactions_checked.action: Monitor blood pressure closely for first 2 weeks; consider reducing lisinopril if systolic <120 mmHg or patient feels dizzy.
No dose adjustment required; monitor CK if muscle symptoms develop.

contraindications.reason: Contraindicated if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² (risk of lactic acidosis). Patient's eGFR not yet known.
contraindications.alternative: Obtain serum creatinine/eGFR before initiating; if eGFR <30, consider lifestyle intervention alone or a DPP‑4 inhibitor.

contraindications.reason: NSAIDs can worsen hypertension, renal function and dyslipidaemia; contraindicated in metabolic syndrome per NICE CG181.
contraindications.alternative: Use paracetamol for analgesia if needed.

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m² for initial prescribing; will order renal function tests before starting metformin.
Full lipid profile (LDL‑C, triglycerides) not available – statin initiated at moderate intensity pending results.
Fasting glucose/HbA1c not available – metformin prescribed conditionally pending confirmation of pre‑diabetes.
QRISK score not calculated – assumed ≥10% based on obesity, hypertension, low HDL; formal calculation will be performed.
Smoking status, alcohol intake, and allergy history not documented – will be assessed at next visit.
Blood pressure reading 132/86 mmHg considered borderline; addition of amlodipine aims to achieve target <140/90 mmHg.
treatment_summary: The plan addresses each component of metabolic syndrome: continue lisinopril for hypertension, add amlodipine to reach BP target, start atorvastatin for lipid reduction, initiate semaglutide for weight loss, and consider metformin if pre‑diabetes is confirmed and renal function is adequate. Monitoring of BP, lipids, renal function, glucose, and weight is outlined, with attention to potential hypotensive interaction between lisinopril and amlodipine. Lifestyle interventions (diet, exercise, sleep‑apnoea therapy) are recommended alongside pharmacotherapy.
